idiom_name: explicit domain types + separate data model + mapper/repository layer
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: keep the domain model in its own module or package that imports nothing from the persistence library, the schema or the transport format; give the storage its own representation (rows, documents, ORM entities or DAO classes) in the infrastructure layer; write one mapper per aggregate whose only job is translating between the two, and let a repository or gateway own loading, hydration and saving. Rehydrate through constructors or factories so invariants are re-established from raw data instead of trusted, and treat stored data as slightly outside the trust boundary. Add the second (persistence) model only where the storage shape genuinely diverges from the domain - a legacy schema, versioned documents, value objects spread over tables; otherwise configure the ORM to map the domain types directly rather than maintaining an extra DAO layer. Keep the dependency arrow pointing inward: the persistence side imports the domain, never the reverse.
code_sketch:
# domain layer: types with behaviour, no storage imports
order = Order(id, lines); order.confirm()      # invariants enforced here
# infrastructure layer: data model + mapper + repository
OrderRow  <->  to_domain(row) / to_row(order)
repo.save(order)                                # hydrate via the constructor
pitfalls: Mapping by field-name convention or reflection: dropped, renamed or mis-ordered fields re-enter the domain unvalidated.
Letting persistence types - rows, ORM entities, query builders, lazy proxies - escape upward through the repository interface.
Introducing a second persistence model as ceremony when the ORM can already map the domain types, doubling maintenance for no gain.
Losing change tracking and transaction scope with the ORM entities, so saves silently happen in a different session or transaction than intended.

Wrong move: adding a column to the data model with no change forced in the explicit mapper -> the new field never reaches the domain and readers see a stale default instead of an error -> make the mapper or its round-trip tests fail loudly when the data-model shape changes.

Wrong move: keeping domain and data models alive side by side and updating both in step through a transaction -> two sources of truth drift and fight over writes -> translate once at the boundary: load into the domain, mutate only the domain, map back on save.
